answer: One concrete defense is stake-anchored identity: each agent locks a slashable deposit before it can trade or vote, so spawning fake agents costs real capital instead of being free. When a gale of suspicious newcomers arrives, the network raises the required stake, making mass identity creation economically suicidal. To keep honest small operators in the game, a juniper-root sponsorship lets established agents vouch for newcomers by co-signing their deposits; both are slashed if the newcomer cheats, so every plume of fake identities still traces back to real money at risk.
